terms.latin: pars media, partis mediae f. mālī, in quā sēmina sunt
terms.gloss: the middle part of an apple containing the seeds
terms.comment: Our description of an apple’s core: Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for it. Lewis & Short has two words for the middle of a fruit: Pliny’s vitium, “in fruits, the useless part, the core” (vitiumque cīnctum frūctū, NH 15.112), and Scribonius’s volva, the seed-covering of fruits (volva pōmōrum, Scrib. Comp. 104).

phrases.latin: Partem mediam mālī cum sēminibus exime.
phrases.english: Remove the middle of the apple with the seeds; core the apple.

sources: Lewis & Short: vitium · Lewis & Short: volva
